name: Working index
concept: A useful directory, with the engineer close at hand.
idea: Harry’s collection of personally useful tools becomes a searchable public index.
type: Arial throughout; compact titles, generous line spacing.
layout: A calm introduction above a searchable six-project index and a strip of real interfaces.
interaction: Search the project index by name, purpose, or category.
strength: Fast to scan; puts engineering substance before presentation.
tradeoff: The least expressive option. The work has to carry the personality.

name: A personal letter
concept: A personal journal, organised around the questions behind the projects.
idea: Harry’s account of engineering, fatherhood, and making becomes a personal letter with working links.
type: Georgia prose and questions, with small Arial project labels. Warm paper and muted red links.
layout: An intimate opening letter flows into six expandable project questions, then pictures and longer notes.
interaction: Open a question to reveal the project behind it; follow its story or unfold the complete gitrove case study.
strength: A personal voice and a useful archive; the questions make the projects approachable.
tradeoff: More reading, with project previews behind native disclosures. A separate picture collection supports visual browsing.

name: Signal press
concept: A software portfolio with the force of a printed poster.
idea: Harry’s name and the names of his own tools become the typography of a software poster.
type: Impact display lettering, with Arial text. Flat colour and tightly set type.
layout: A large two-line name on an acid-yellow field, then oversized project names interrupted by real screens.
interaction: Filter the project roll by all work, developer tools, or home projects.
strength: Most assertive; memorable at a glance and distinct from a typical engineering portfolio.
tradeoff: The poster voice is louder than the quiet personal practice. It needs restraint in the case studies.

name: Dot matrix
concept: A software portfolio drawn as a living print specimen.
idea: Harry’s initials and his real product screens become a language of dots, pixels, and readable software.
type: Arial throughout; a custom bitmap monogram carries the expressive role.
layout: A wide two-part opening with a large raster identity specimen, followed by paired product prints and a quiet case-study reading surface.
interaction: Switch actual project interfaces between dot-matrix prints and their original screenshots.
strength: Playful and tactile without relying on retro window chrome; the visual language is made from the person and the software.
tradeoff: Halftone images communicate character rather than interface detail; the original-screen switch is essential for close reading.

references.title: A Survey of Life-Forms, J. H. Conway

name: Project atlas
concept: An engineering practice, seen through its actual materials.
idea: Harry’s six real projects and their listed technologies become a readable project atlas.
type: Arial throughout; large names, compact tabular figures, white-on-cobalt data.
layout: A stable introductory column beside a large incidence matrix, followed by real interface images and a full project reading panel.
interaction: Choose a technology to highlight the matching projects and read an exact count from the six-project inventory.
strength: Makes the engineering practice tangible and explorable, using real relationships rather than decorative charts.
tradeoff: More analytical than the personal letter. Five selected technologies are a useful lens, not a complete list of everything each project uses.
